reasons.message: bypassPermissions in agent frontmatter ignored because permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode is set (P4).
Settings layers disagree on permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode; the value comes from the highest-priority layer that sets it (S1). See this reason's source.
permissions.allow entry "Bash(npm run test:unit)" has no effect: a settings layer denies "Bash", and a deny rule is not overridden at any level (S2, S5). See this reason's source for the deny entry.
permissions.allow entry "Write" has no effect: a settings layer denies "Write", and a deny rule is not overridden at any level (S2, S5). See this reason's source for the deny entry.
permissions.allow entry "*" is an unanchored glob and grants nothing (S4).
permissions.allow entry "Bash(npm run test:*)" has no effect: a settings layer denies "Bash", and a deny rule is not overridden at any level (S2, S5). See this reason's source for the deny entry.
permissions.allow entry "mcp__*" is an unanchored glob and grants nothing (S4).
permissions.allow entry "mcp__github(issues)" uses the bracket syntax, which MCP permission rules do not support, so it grants nothing (S3).

permissions.allow entry "Read(/src/**)" narrows individual invocations of Read rather than the tool itself; this product resolves what the platform applies and does not evaluate rule arguments (§2.3), so the effect of this rule is unknown.
Matrix entry "settings.pathRules" rests on non-[doc] fact(s) S7 but has no fixture-level evidence; enforcement is unknown (SPEC §8.2).

permissions.allow entry "WebFetch(domain:example.com)" narrows individual invocations of WebFetch rather than the tool itself; this product resolves what the platform applies and does not evaluate rule arguments (§2.3), so the effect of this rule is unknown.
Matrix entry "settings.webFetchRules" rests on non-[doc] fact(s) S8 but has no fixture-level evidence; enforcement is unknown (SPEC §8.2).
permissions.deny entry "Bash" removes the tool from the session entirely (S5); settings deny rules are applied last and are not overridden by agent frontmatter or by a bypass permission mode (S2).
